subproblems.title: Integrals over finite sets with respect to H⁰ = μHE[0]
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let F be a finite subset of ℝ^P (a Finset), let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be any function and g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] any function (no measurability is assumed). Then the Bochner integral of f over F with respect to Mathlib's normalized 0-dimensional Hausdorff measure H⁰ = μHE[0] equals Σ_{x∈F} f(x). Likewise the lower Lebesgue integral of g over F with respect to μHE[0] equals Σ_{x∈F} g(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (F : Finset (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (g : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞), (∫ x in (F : Set (Euclid P)), f x ∂μHE[0]) = ∑ x ∈ F, f x ∧ (∫⁻ x in (F : Set (Euclid P)), g x ∂μHE[0]) = ∑ x ∈ F, g x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the supplied proof of the selected parent dtc_bc_tc_cl_closure_degree_zero (H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure: euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero, hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton) and the finite-set integrals used in its steps 1 and 6. Simon's printed proof of Ch. 6, Theorem 8.2 (book/chapter-06.txt line 2323) only says that "the theorem is trivial in case n = 0", so this argument is extracted and specialized from the parent-supplied proof (Part III, CL(0)). This child is the declaration cbrz_finset_integral_hausdorff_zero, already accepted (candidate commit fc243d0a) with exactly this frozen Lean type and reused here by name; the proof below is a complete proof of the statement.

1. Normalisation. Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero gives μHE[0] = μH[0] on ℝ^P; rewrite both goals with it. Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton gives μH[0]{x} = 1 for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Singletons of ℝ^P are Borel, hence measurable (MeasurableSingletonClass). So it suffices to prove both identities for μ := μH[0].
2. Integrability of f on F. As sets, F = ⋃_{x∈F} {x} (Set.biUnion_of_singleton). For each x ∈ F, f is integrable on {x} with respect to μ by Mathlib integrableOn_singleton, because ‖f(x)‖ₑ < ∞ (f(x) is a real number) and μ{x} = 1 < ∞. No measurability of f is needed: on {x} the restricted measure is μ{x}·δ_x, and f agrees a.e. with the constant f(x). Integrability on each piece of a finite union gives integrability on the union (Mathlib integrableOn_finite_biUnion, the index set F being finite). Hence f is integrable on F.
3. Bochner integral. With the integrability of step 2, Mathlib MeasureTheory.setIntegral_finset gives ∫_F f dμ = Σ_{x∈F} μ.real{x} • f(x). Here μ.real{x} = (μ{x}).toReal = 1 (measureReal_def), so ∫_F f dμ = Σ_{x∈F} f(x). This is the first identity.
4. Lower integral. For a measure with measurable singletons and a finset F, Mathlib MeasureTheory.lintegral_finset gives ∫⁻_F g dμ = Σ_{x∈F} g(x)·μ{x} for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞]; no measurability of g is needed. Since μ{x} = 1, this equals Σ_{x∈F} g(x). This is the second identity.
5. Steps 1–4 prove both identities for μHE[0]. ∎

Reuse evidence (not part of the mathematical argument): the Lean proof committed at fc243d0a96fcd9abfe56b146339fc11e52fdf627 declares Submission.cbrz_finset_integral_hausdorff_zero with exactly this type; in this decomposition session it was extracted verbatim from that commit and compiled together with the other four reused declarations and the selected parent's assembly after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission` in the replayed contract scope (Lean v4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 25730c7c, SimonGMT 2b366308); `#print axioms` reported only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
proof_key_steps: μHE[0] = μH[0] (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) and μH[0]{x} = 1 (hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton); singletons are measurable
f is integrable on each singleton (integrableOn_singleton), hence on the finite union F (integrableOn_finite_biUnion)
Bochner integral over a finset = Σ μ.real{x}·f(x) = Σ f(x) (setIntegral_finset)
lower integral over a finset = Σ g(x)·μ{x} = Σ g(x) (lintegral_finset)

subproblems.title: Limits of bounded weighted point sums in a compact set are finite integer point sums
subproblems.statement: Let P, C ∈ ℕ and let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact. Let N : ℕ → ℕ, w : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ and x : ℕ → ℕ → ℝ^P satisfy x_{j,l} ∈ K and w_{j,l} ≠ 0 whenever l < N_j, and Σ_{l<N_j} |w_{j,l}| ≤ C for every j. Let ι be a type, and for k ∈ ι let g_k : ℝ^P → ℝ be continuous and t_k ∈ ℝ, such that Σ_{l<N_j} w_{j,l} g_k(x_{j,l}) → t_k as j → ∞ for every k. Then there are M ∈ ℕ, v : ℕ → ℤ and y : ℕ → ℝ^P with y_l ∈ K for l < M and t_k = Σ_{l<M} v_l g_k(y_l) for every k ∈ ι.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid P)) (C : ℕ) (N : ℕ → ℕ) (w : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ) (x : ℕ → ℕ → Euclid P) (ι : Type) (g : ι → Euclid P → ℝ) (t : ι → ℝ), IsCompact K → (∀ j l, l < N j → x j l ∈ K) → (∀ j l, l < N j → w j l ≠ 0) → (∀ j, (∑ l ∈ Finset.range (N j), (w j l).natAbs) ≤ C) → (∀ k, Continuous (g k)) → (∀ k, Tendsto (fun j => ∑ l ∈ Finset.range (N j), (w j l : ℝ) * g k (x j l)) atTop (𝓝 (t k))) → ∃ (M : ℕ) (v : ℕ → ℤ) (y : ℕ → Euclid P), (∀ l < M, y l ∈ K) ∧ ∀ k, t k = ∑ l ∈ Finset.range M, (v l : ℝ) * g k (y l)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–5 of the supplied proof of the selected parent dtc_bc_tc_cl_closure_degree_zero: N_j ≤ c and the sign vectors take finitely many values and B̄_{2r}(x₀)^N is compact, so a subsequence has constant count, constant signs and convergent points x_{j,i} → y_i, and T(a) = lim_j T_j(a) = Σ_i ε_i⟨a(y_i)⟩ by continuity. subproblems.title: A finite set has approximate tangent space {0} in dimension 0 at each of its points
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let F ⊆ ℝ^P be a finite set and let y ∈ F. Then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 F y ⊥ holds (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4 with n = 0). Explicitly: the zero subspace ⊥ = {0} has dimension 0, and for every compactly supported continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫_{η_{y,ρ}(F)} f dH⁰ → ∫_{{0}} f dH⁰ = f(0) as ρ → 0 with ρ > 0. Here η_{y,ρ}(z) = ρ⁻¹(z − y) is SimonGMT blowUpMap y ρ and H⁰ = μHE[0].

We take Q = ⊥ = {0}.

1. Dimension. finrank ℝ (⊥ : Submodule ℝ ℝ^P) = 0 (Mathlib finrank_bot). Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ).
2. Limit value. The carrier of ⊥ is {0} (Submodule.bot_coe), the coercion of the finset {0}. The first identity of the sibling theorem cbrz_finset_integral_hausdorff_zero (count_integral), applied to the finset {0}, gives ∫_⊥ f dH⁰ = f(0).
3. Support radius. tsupport f is compact (f.hasCompactSupport), hence bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ B̄_R(0) for some R ∈ ℝ (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall). Put R₀ := max(R, 0) + 1 > 0. If ‖z‖ ≥ R₀, then ‖z‖ > R, so z ∉ tsupport f and f(z) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport).
4. Separation radius. F ∖ {y} is finite, hence closed, and does not contain y. Its complement is therefore an open neighbourhood of y, so there is δ > 0 with B_δ(y) ∩ (F ∖ {y}) = ∅ (Metric.isOpen_iff). Thus ‖z − y‖ ≥ δ for every z ∈ F with z ≠ y (vacuous if F = {y}).
5. Fix ρ ∈ (0, δ/R₀); this interval belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 because δ/R₀ > 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). The image η_{y,ρ}(F) is finite (Set.Finite.image); regard it as a finset. The first identity of the sibling theorem cbrz_finset_integral_hausdorff_zero gives ∫_{η_{y,ρ}(F)} f dH⁰ = Σ_{w ∈ η_{y,ρ}(F)} f(w).

subproblems.title: Degree-0 integer multiplicity currents are finite weighted point sums on compactly contained sets
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and U, B ⊆ ℝ^P. Let R be a degree-0 IMRep in U representing S ∈ 𝒟_0(U), and suppose B ⊂⊂ U (closure B is compact and contained in U). Then there are N ∈ ℕ, w : ℕ → ℤ and x : ℕ → ℝ^P such that: x_l ∈ B and w_l ≠ 0 for every l < N; Σ_{l<N} |w_l| ≤ R.measure(B) in [0, ∞]; and S(ω) = Σ_{l<N} w_l ⟨ω(x_l)⟩ for every ω ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ B. Here ⟨α⟩ := α(e) is the value of a 0-covector on the empty family e = (fun i => i.elim0).

Put ⟨α⟩ := α(e) for α ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, 0). H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) and H⁰{p} = 1 (hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Let K := closure B; since B ⊂⊂ U, K is compact and K ⊆ U.

1. Local finiteness. By the field locallyIntegrable_mult, I := ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ < ∞. Suppose M ∩ K were infinite. Pick n ∈ ℕ with I < n (ENNReal.exists_nat_gt) and an n-element finset F' ⊆ M ∩ K (Set.Infinite.exists_subset_card_eq). Since θ ≥ 1 on M (field mult_pos), n = Σ_{x∈F'} 1 ≤ Σ_{x∈F'} θ(x) = ∫⁻_{F'} θ dH⁰ (lower-integral identity of the sibling theorem cbrz_finset_integral_hausdorff_zero) ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ = I (lintegral_mono_set), contradicting I < n. M is measurable and G ⊆ M, so Mathlib setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero gives ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH⁰ = ∫_G θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH⁰. 5. Listing. Let N := #G and enumerate G by the bijection Finset.equivFin: x_l := G.equivFin.symm(l) for l < N, and x_l := 0 for l ≥ N. Hence Σ_{l<N} |w_l| = Σ_{p∈G} θ(p) ≤ R.measure(B) by step 4, and for ω as in step 3, S(ω) = Σ_{p∈G} ε(p)θ(p)⟨ω(p)⟩ = Σ_{l<N} w_l⟨ω(x_l)⟩. ∎

subproblems.title: Finite integer combinations of point evaluations are integer multiplicity 0-currents
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and S ∈ 𝒟_0(V) (GeometricCurrentOn V 0). Let M ∈ ℕ, v : ℕ → ℤ and y : ℕ → ℝ^P; the points y_l need not lie in V. So the nonzero terms are indexed by G (Finset.sum_filter_of_ne), and S(ω) = Σ_{p∈G} m(p)⟨ω(p)⟩.

Define carrier := G; mult := the indicator of G applied to p ↦ |m(p)| ∈ ℕ (Int.natAbs); s := the indicator of G applied to p ↦ sign(m(p)) ∈ ℝ (Int.sign, cast to ℝ); orient(p) := s(p)·ev.
